note: The fuzz target uses the submitted raw bytes as a WebAssembly module and parses them into an AST module.
The parsed module is validated before AOT compilation; the candidate contains a non-void function body that becomes unreachable before producing its declared return value.
Validation creates the outer function control frame with the function's declared return types as the frame end types.
After an unreachable instruction, the validator records that the active control frame is unreachable.
At the end of the function expression, validation checks the declared end types even though the value stack has no concrete return operand.
When the validation stack is at the frame height and the frame is unreachable, validation fabricates an unknown value type instead of rejecting the missing return operand.
The fabricated unknown type is treated as matching the expected function return type, so validation succeeds without a concrete value.
The validated module is then handed to the AOT compiler.
AOT compilation creates an outer return block for the function but does not create a concrete LLVM value corresponding to the validator's fabricated unknown return operand.
After compiling the instruction stream, the compiler emits the function epilogue return even though the compiler value stack lacks the declared non-void return value.
For a scalar non-void return type, compileReturn unconditionally pops from the compiler stack; the missing operand makes stackPop read from an empty vector and triggers the sanitizer crash.
